seo.title: AI Mode Inline Links: Google's Update Explained
seo.meta_description: Google is adding more AI Mode inline links, an official websites section and news carousels. What the update means for Orange County businesses.

h1: Google's New AI Mode Inline Links: What Orange County Businesses Should Know
answer: Google's October 2026 update adds more AI Mode inline links inside AI answers, shows them higher up, tests a dedicated section for official websites and expands news carousels. For businesses in Anaheim and Orange County, it means a clear, quotable page has a better chance of being the link people click inside an AI answer.
key_takeaways: Google is adding more inline links to AI Mode and AI Overviews.
Inline links will appear higher in responses more often.
Google is testing a section that highlights official websites.
Preferred Sources use grew more than 7x this year, Google says.
Clear, specific pages are the ones worth linking to.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.body_html: On October 15, 2026, Google announced updates across its AI search features, AI Mode and AI Overviews, aimed at helping people explore the web. The changes include more inline links inside AI responses, inline links shown higher up, a test of a dedicated section for official websites, wider rollout of carousels for timely articles, more prominent related links with image thumbnails and clickable creator and publisher names on video results.

sections.heading: What inline links are
sections.body_html: Google defines inline links as links embedded in words or phrases in an AI response. Instead of a list of sources at the side or bottom, the link sits right inside the sentence that makes the claim. Google says it has made "continued and substantial increases" to inline links in its AI experiences and is now showing them higher in responses more frequently, so key sources are easy to click while someone is reading.

sections.heading: Why this matters for clicks
sections.body_html: Clicks from AI answers have been scarce. In Pew Research Center's March 2025 browsing data from 900 U.S. adults, people clicked a link inside Google's AI summary on just 1% of visits that showed one, and clicked any search result on 8% of those visits, compared with 15% when no summary appeared. More visible inline links are Google's attempt to change that pattern. Whether it works will show up in your own Search Console data over the coming months.

sections.heading: The official websites section
sections.body_html: Google says that sometimes there are only one or two official places on the web to complete a task or get exact information. It is testing a display that surfaces these links in a dedicated section at the top of a response, with context about why each link is useful. For a local business, the practical lesson is simple: make sure your own website is the obvious official source for your business, with your services, prices, hours, booking and contact details stated clearly.

sections.heading: Preferred Sources are growing
sections.body_html: Google reports that the number of people using its Preferred Sources feature has grown by more than 7x since the start of the year. Preferred Sources lets people choose sites they want to see more of, and Google says its expanding news carousels also highlight those sources. For Orange County publishers and businesses that publish regular, useful updates, it is a reason to encourage loyal readers to add you.

sections.heading: What this means in Orange County
sections.body_html: Orange County had 3,186,989 residents in the 2020 census, and its three largest cities, Anaheim, Santa Ana and Irvine, each have more than 300,000 people. That is a lot of local searches for services, from "emergency plumber in Anaheim" to "best dentist in Irvine". When Google answers those with AI, the businesses that get the inline link are the ones whose page states the answer clearly enough to quote.

sections.heading: Step 1: write quotable sentences
sections.body_html: An inline link attaches to a phrase. Pages that make one clear claim per sentence are easier to link than pages full of slogans. Put direct answers near the top of each page: what you do, where, for whom, at what price range and how fast. Use specific nouns and numbers you can stand behind, and source any statistic you quote.

sections.heading: Step 2: be the official source
sections.body_html: Make your website the definitive place for facts about your business. A clear About page, a services page per service, a contact page with your Anaheim or Orange County address, and Organization or LocalBusiness structured data that matches. Keep your Google Business Profile consistent with the site. If a directory or old listing disagrees with your site, fix it.

sections.heading: Step 3: publish timely, useful updates
sections.body_html: Google says the carousels for timely articles are expanding to more locations and languages, and that they make timely articles visible on a wider range of queries. A business blog that covers real local news in your field, such as new regulations, seasonal demand or local events, gives Google something current to show. Publish only what is accurate and genuinely useful; volume alone does not help.

sections.heading: Step 4: claim creator profiles if you make video
sections.body_html: Google is testing clickable creator and publisher names on video results in AI Mode that link to their Search profiles. If your business publishes video, for example how-to clips or project walkthroughs, look at Google's information about Search profiles and whether you are eligible.

sections.heading: What not to do
sections.body_html: Do not rewrite every page into short, keyword-stuffed fragments to chase links. Google's guidance for its AI features is that the same fundamentals apply as for Search: content made for people, crawlable and helpful. Mass-producing thin pages to catch AI links risks Google's scaled content abuse policy.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Google is putting more links inside its AI answers and testing a spot for official websites. For businesses in Anaheim and across Orange County, the opportunity is to be the clearest, most official source for your own facts and the most useful source for your field.

faqs.q: What are inline links in AI Mode?
faqs.a: Links embedded in words or phrases inside an AI response, so readers can click the source right where a claim is made.

faqs.q: When did Google announce more inline links?
faqs.a: Google announced the update on October 15, 2026, covering AI Mode and AI Overviews.

faqs.q: What is the official websites section in AI Mode?
faqs.a: A display Google is testing that highlights the one or two official sites for a task at the top of a response, with context about each link.
A feature that lets people choose sites they want to see more of. Google says its use has grown more than 7x since the start of 2026.

faqs.q: Do inline links mean more traffic?
faqs.a: They may help. Pew's 2025 data showed only 1% of visits with an AI summary included a click on a link in it, so more visible links could change that. Check your own Search Console data.

faqs.q: How do I get my site used as an inline link?
faqs.a: Write clear, specific, sourced sentences, make your site the official source for your own facts and keep pages crawlable.

faqs.q: Does this update affect AI Overviews too?
faqs.a: Yes. Google said the updates apply across its AI search features, including AI Overviews.

faqs.q: Should I change all my pages for this update?
faqs.a: No. Improve clarity and facts on important pages. Mass-produced thin pages risk Google's spam policies.
